input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight run on the p16 candidate. I traced every limitation of all 17 claims (1–10 apparatus, 11–13 installed assembly, 14–17 method), every entry in the 28-row numeral ledger (10–66), every numbered part and relationship in the Field, Summary, Brief Description and Detailed Description, and all six figure briefs (FIG. 1–6, including geometry sections, schematic declarations, sheet-text rules and numeral placement targets) back to affirmative USER passages in input/disclosure.md and the single USER message in input/conversation.md; input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority and no-government-support formalities. The substantive ledger is supported: split reusable clamp, two substantially semicircular halves, hinge end and releasable latch end, three radial jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads that avoid a tool-specific pipe diameter, segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment carried by each half, complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by frame closure, followers in oblique slots, wedge on the latch bearing on a ring drive face, limited stroke, synchronized inward travel, outward-biasing carriage springs, holding position plus over-center position, force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge, visible indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range, the express statement that the indicator does not measure pipe diameter, the install/remove sequences, and the optional mounting boss outside the annular guide that does not participate in synchronization. Claim 11's "installed clamp assembly", claim 6's equal inward travel, claims 3 and 9's negative and retraction limitations, and claims 8/13/17's mounting-boss limitations all trace to exact disclosure sentences. I confirmed the draft contains none of the "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface" matter that appears only in the YOU passage of conversation.md, that Background prior-art characterizations assert no invention structure, that each numeral denotes exactly one part and appears in at least one brief and in the description, that FIG. 1/2/3/5/6 agree on three carriages/slideways/slots at top, lower right and lower left, that FIG. 3 and FIG. 6 agree on segment 32 upper and 34 lower with 44/46 at the left (hinge) junction and 48/50 at the right (latch) junction consistent with FIG. 1's hinge-left, latch-right layout, and that no section lines, drafting notes, placeholders, open questions or unresolved alternatives remain anywhere in the text or briefs. Depiction-convention language ("shown schematically", "outline is a depiction convention", near-side material omitted) stays confined to the figure briefs; the application text and claims remain shape-neutral and contain no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening. Two defects remain and are reported: (1) FIG-6 verbalizes a narrow clearance between the two segment end faces at each junction, an untraced contact-topology statement about a functional drive-face joint that the disclosure, FIG-3 and the Brief Description all describe as abutting/engaged when the frame is closed; and (2) FIG-3 refers to the ring drive face 54 as lying "at the latch end" without identifying which junction is the latch end, leaving numeral 54's circumferential position undetermined relative to FIG-1 and FIG-6. Both findings carry filing-clean automatic fixes confined to the figure briefs; no application text needs added shape or optional-embodiment language. As the brief itself notes, the supplied prior art may be incomplete, but no patentability question was assessed here.

findings.title: FIG-6 draws and verbalizes a clearance between segment drive faces the source says abut
findings.where: figures/FIG-6.md, left-junction and right-junction geometry bullets; cross-checked against figures/FIG-3.md and draft/07-drawings.md
findings.detail: The FIG-6 brief instructs that the two end faces at each junction be drawn "side by side across the band with a narrow clearance between them" and then explains that clearance as a depiction convention. Clearance versus contact at a functional drive-face joint is contact topology, which is substantive even in a schematic view, and no inventor passage discloses any gap between the segment end faces. The disclosure affirmatively describes the opposite condition: the faces come together on closure and couple the segments. The brief also contradicts itself and the rest of the application: its own view line says the sheet shows "the end faces that abut one another", FIG-3 says "the end face of the upper segment and the end face of the lower segment abut one another", the Brief Description says FIG. 6 shows "the end faces that abut at the junctions between the segments", and the Detailed Description says closing the halves "brings the first hinge-end drive face 44 into engagement with the second hinge-end drive face 46". Separate lead lines for 44, 46, 48 and 50 do not require a gap; two lines drawn in contact remain two separately identifiable pieces of line work.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-6.md): "the two lines lying side by side across the band with a narrow clearance between them" and "The narrow clearance is a depiction convention adopted so that the two end faces read separately at this scale; the end faces abut one another when the frame halves are closed." Nearest source passage (input/disclosure.md): "When the halves close, complementary drive faces at the hinge and latch ends couple the segments so that they move as one ring." No disclosure or conversation passage anywhere describes a clearance, gap or spacing between the end faces; the disclosure never separates the faces except by opening the frame ("To remove the clamp, releasing the latch...").
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-6.md, delete the phrase "with a narrow clearance between them" from the left-junction bullet and the phrase "with the same narrow clearance between them" from the right-junction bullet, replacing each with "the two lines meeting one another in contact so that no gap appears between them"; and delete the sentence "The narrow clearance is a depiction convention adopted so that the two end faces read separately at this scale; the end faces abut one another when the frame halves are closed." Keep the requirement that each end face is its own plain straight line across the full width of the band so that 44, 46, 48 and 50 each retain their own lead line ending on their own end-face line. No change to draft/07-drawings.md or draft/08-detailed-description.md is needed.

findings.title: FIG-3 places the ring drive face 54 "at the latch end" without identifying which junction is the latch end
findings.where: figures/FIG-3.md, drive-face geometry bullet and numeral placement target for 54
findings.detail: FIG-3 divides the ring by "one at the left and one at the right" junctions but never states which of the two is the hinge-end junction and which is the latch-end junction. It then locates the ring drive face, and numeral 54, only as being "at the latch end of the ring". The latch end is fixed elsewhere in the set: FIG-1 places the latch at the right break and the hinge at the left break, and FIG-6 assigns the latch-end drive faces 48 and 50 to the right junction and the hinge-end drive faces 44 and 46 to the left junction. As written, FIG-3 can be rendered with 54 adjacent to the left junction, which would put the ring drive face at the hinge end and contradict FIG-1, FIG-4 (where the wedge of the latch meets the drive face) and FIG-6. This is an internal-consistency gap in the brief, not an unsupported technical assertion: the wedge is carried by the latch, so the ring drive face at the latch end is compelled by the disclosed drive path.
findings.evidence: Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md geometry): "A short plain drive face on the band at the latch end of the ring, where the wedge of the latch acts on the ring." Candidate (figures/FIG-3.md numerals): "54: the short plain drive face on the band at the latch end." Compare figures/FIG-1.md: "At the right break, a latch drawn as a compact rectangular body..." and figures/FIG-6.md: "48: placed outside the ring near the right junction and above it... 50: placed outside the ring near the right junction and below it", with draft/numerals.md identifying 48 and 50 as the first and second latch-end drive faces. Source (input/disclosure.md): "Closing the latch drives a wedge against a drive face of the cam ring."
findings.fix: In figures/FIG-3.md, add to the junction bullet: "The junction at the right of the ring is the latch end junction and the junction at the left is the hinge end junction, in the same orientation as FIG. 1 and FIG. 6." Change the drive-face bullet to read "A short plain drive face on the band adjacent to the right, latch end, junction, where the wedge of the latch acts on the ring." and change the numeral target to "54: the short plain drive face on the band adjacent to the right, latch end, junction." Optionally add the same orientation sentence to figures/FIG-6.md for its "drive face on the band at the latch end" bullet.
